key_insight: ALPS is a pretrained visual encoder designed to represent physical state, align with language, and support pixel reconstruction—all through one shared set of image patch tokens.
problem_solved: Existing visual encoders typically support only one or two of these capabilities, limiting their ability to serve as a unified foundation for world-model prediction, instruction, and inspection.
method: Encode visual inputs into a shared set of patch tokens.
Unify physical-state information, native language alignment, and pixel reconstruction within that representation.
Provide a common visual foundation for world models that predict outcomes, follow instructions, and reconstruct images.
impact: A unified encoder could reduce the need for separate visual representations across world-model tasks. The provided abstract is incomplete and includes no experimental results, so performance gains cannot be assessed.
